title: EmbodiedCLBench: Evaluating Continual Learning for Self-Evolving Embodied Agents
title_zh: EmbodiedCLBench：评估自演化智能体的持续学习能力

paragraphs.en: Continual learning requires models to accumulate past experience and transfer it to new tasks. Despite substantial research on continual learning, existing work remains largely confined to non-embodied settings, without extending to embodied environments. To address this gap, we introduce EmbodiedCLBench , the first benchmark in embodied simulation for evaluating the continual learning capability of self-evolving agents. With compositional generalization as the core evaluation principle, our benchmark evaluates whether agents can first learn from basic tasks and then recombine the acquired skills to solve complex, unseen advanced tasks. Based on EmbodiedCLBench , we conduct extensive experiments across multiple agent harnesses and learning methods, revealing consistent limitations and distinctive behaviors. Our results show that while advanced tasks can be hardly solved under zero-shot setting, the experience from basic tasks enables consistent improvement. Such benefit from the experience remains stable even if the task complexity increases. However, this improvement does not scale accordingly with the number of learning samples, and current agents cannot extract meaningful information from additional experience. Collectively, our findings highlight continual learning as a fundamental yet underexplored capability, and our benchmark offers valuable resources for designing effective self-evolving agents in embodied environments. Our code and dataset are available at https://pku-value-lab.github.io/EmbodiedCLBench-homepage .

paragraphs.en: Self-evolving agents ( Gao et al., 2025 ; Fang et al., 2025 ) can accumulate experience from past interactions and progressively enhance their task performance without additional human supervision. Such agents are capable of retaining and transferring skills across tasks over time, a capability broadly termed continual learning ( Zheng et al., 2025b ) . This capability is particularly important for embodied intelligence ( Liu et al., 2025a ; Yifan et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2025b ) , where agents are expected to operate in complex, ever-changing physical environments that cannot be fully anticipated at training time. It is therefore important to develop a principled approach for evaluating the capability to learn from prior interactions and transfers the acquired skills to new tasks.

paragraphs.en: Existing benchmarks in continual learning and embodied intelligence partially address this evaluation goal. Research on continual learning has largely focused on non-embodied settings, including knowledge-intensive tasks ( Gao et al., 2026 ) , interactive digital environments ( Jiang et al., 2026 ) , and long-term simulated worlds ( Cai et al., 2025 ) . These platforms do not capture the spatial complexity and physical constraints inherent in embodied tasks. Meanwhile, embodied benchmarks evaluate capabilities such as scene perception ( Wang et al., 2024 ) , visual navigation ( Anderson et al., 2018 ) , robotic manipulation ( Gu et al., 2023 ) , and long-horizon task planning ( Shridhar et al., 2020 ) , but are not specifically designed to assess continual learning. Therefore, there remains a lack of a dedicated benchmark for evaluating whether self-evolving agents can accumulate experience and transfer it to solve novel tasks in embodied environments.
paragraphs.zh: 持续学习和具身智能领域的现有基准测试部分实现了这一评估目标。 持续学习的研究主要聚焦于非具身场景，包括知识密集型任务（Gao 等人，2026）、交互式数字环境（Jiang 等人，2026）以及长期模拟世界（Cai 等人，2025）。 这些平台未能体现具身任务中固有的空间复杂性和物理约束。 与此同时，具身基准测试评估了场景感知（Wang 等人，2024）、视觉导航（Anderson 等人，2018）、机器人操作（Gu 等人，2023）以及长期任务规划（Shridhar 等人，2020）等能力，但并未专门设计用于评估持续学习。 因此，目前仍缺乏一个专门的基准测试，用以评估自我演化的智能体是否能够在具身环境中积累经验并将其迁移到解决新任务中。

paragraphs.en: To address this gap, we introduce EmbodiedCLBench , the first benchmark in embodied simulation for evaluating the continual learning capability of self-evolving agents. As illustrated in Figure 1 , our design stems from compositional generalization ( Furuta et al., 2023 ; Guo et al., 2025 ) . Instead of learning every new task from scratch, a self-evolving agent should recombine previously acquired skill elements to solve novel, unseen tasks. We thus consider compositional generalization as a principled way to measure agent continual learning capability. Specifically, we first assign a set of basic tasks for the agent to execute and learn the skills. We then test whether the agent can effectively leverage such experience to solve unseen advanced tasks that require recombining the learned skills. From this perspective, basic tasks serve as test-time learning ( Sun et al., 2020 ; Liu et al., 2021 ) data for the agent to build experience before attempting advanced tasks. To this end, EmbodiedCLBench organizes tasks into three compositional levels: (1) atomic actions from TongSim ( Sun et al., 2025 ) , representing basic object–action interactions; (2) basic tasks, with each composing a small number of atomic actions into practical household operations across multiple categories; and (3) advanced tasks, with each combining elements from multiple basic-task categories.
paragraphs.zh: 为了解决这一空白，我们提出了 EmbodiedCLBench——首个用于评估自我进化智能体持续学习能力的具身模拟基准。 如图 1 所示，我们的设计源于组合泛化（Furuta 等人，2023；Guo 等人，2025）。 自我进化的智能体不应从头学习每一项新任务，而应重新组合先前获得的技能要素，以解决新颖且未见过的任务。 因此，我们将组合泛化视为衡量智能体持续学习能力的一种有原则的方法。 具体来说，我们首先为智能体分配一组基础任务，以便其执行并学习相关技能。 接着，我们测试智能体能否有效利用这些经验，解决需要重新组合所学技能的未见过的进阶任务。 从这个角度来看，基础任务充当了测试时学习（Sun 等人，2020；Liu 等人，2021）的数据，供智能体在尝试进阶任务前积累经验。 为此，EmbodiedCLBench 将任务组织为三个组合层级：（1）来自 TongSim（Sun 等人，2025）的原子动作，代表基本的对象-动作交互；（2）基础任务，每个任务由少量原子动作组合而成，涵盖多个类别的实际家庭操作；以及（3）进阶任务，每个任务融合了来自多个基础任务类别的要素。

paragraphs.en: Based on EmbodiedCLBench , we conduct extensive evaluation across multiple agent harnesses (e.g., OpenClaw and Codex ) and learning methods (In-Context Learning and Skill Learning). Our results reveal several notable and, in some cases, unexpected findings. First , while advanced tasks can hardly be solved in the zero-shot setting, agents with experience from related basic tasks achieve substantially higher success rates. This validates that experience from simpler tasks can be effectively transferred to unseen, harder tasks. Second , the performance gain over zero-shot agents remains at a stable level as task complexity increases. This suggests that continual learning capability is not sensitive to task difficulty. Third , the improvement from learning does not scale accordingly with the number of learning samples. A single basic task significantly improves performance, and additional samples yield no consistent further improvement. Fourth , past experience facilitates the decision behavior of agents by selecting more meaningful actions with fewer unexecutable ones.
paragraphs.zh: 基于 EmbodiedCLBench，我们在多种智能体框架（例如 OpenClaw 和 Codex）以及学习方法（上下文学习和技能学习）上进行了广泛评估。 我们的结果揭示了几项值得注意的、在某些情况下甚至出乎意料的发现。 首先，尽管高级任务在零样本设置下几乎无法解决，但拥有相关基础任务经验的智能体却能取得显著更高的成功率。 这验证了来自更简单任务的经验可以有效迁移到未见过且更难的任务中。 其次，随着任务复杂度的增加，与零样本智能体相比的性能提升仍保持在一个稳定水平。 这表明持续学习能力对任务难度并不敏感。 第三，学习带来的改进并不会随着学习样本数量的增加而相应扩大。 单个基础任务就能显著提升性能，而更多样本并未带来持续且一致的性能提升。 第四，过往经验通过减少不可执行动作的选择、更多地选取更有意义的动作，从而促进了智能体的决策行为。

paragraphs.en: We introduce EmbodiedCLBench , the first benchmark in embodied simulation for evaluating the continual learning capability of self-evolving agents.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 EmbodiedCLBench——首个用于评估自我进化智能体持续学习能力的具身模拟基准测试。

paragraphs.en: Our key innovation lies in leveraging compositional generalization as a principled way to construct tasks, design evaluation protocols, and evaluate continual learning capability.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的核心创新在于利用组合泛化作为构建任务、设计评估协议以及评估持续学习能力的一种有原则的方法。

paragraphs.en: We conduct a comprehensive evaluation across multiple agent harnesses and learning methods, revealing limitations of current agents and providing insights for future design.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在多种智能体框架和学习方法上进行了全面评估，揭示了当前智能体的局限性，并为未来的设计提供了参考。

paragraphs.en: Evaluating continual learning capabilities has become an increasingly active topic for LLMs and agents ( Gao et al., 2025 ; Fang et al., 2025 ; Zheng et al., 2025b ) . Existing benchmarks span several distinct domains. In knowledge-intensive tasks, prior work evaluates whether agents can effectively transfer procedural experience across coding, reasoning, and question-answering tasks ( Gao et al., 2026 ; Wu et al., 2024 ; Shu et al., 2026 ) . In interactive digital environments, benchmarks test continual learning capabilities in web automation, operating systems, and knowledge graphs ( Jiang et al., 2026 ; Zheng et al., 2025a ) . In long-term simulated environments, benchmarks model persistent virtual worlds where past behaviors continuously shape future states and decisions ( Cai et al., 2025 ) . Another major direction focuses on skill-centric evolution, studying whether agents can abstract reusable skills from experience and transfer them across tasks ( Zhong et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ; Guan et al., 2026 ; Lei et al., 2026 ) . Despite this progress, these benchmarks primarily operate in digital or symbolic environments, leaving continual learning in embodied scenarios largely unexplored.

paragraphs.en: Embodied AI benchmarks evaluate the capabilities ranging from perception to long-horizon task execution ( Liu et al., 2025a ; Yifan et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2025b ) . At the perception level, benchmarks test 3D scene understanding ( Wang et al., 2024 ) , spatial reasoning ( Du et al., 2024 ) , physical world understanding ( Chow et al., 2025 ) , and scene dynamics ( Wang et al., 2025 ) . For navigation, the field has progressed from language-conditioned navigation ( Anderson et al., 2018 ; Ku et al., 2020 ) to sound-guided navigation Liu et al. (2026) , object grounding ( Qi et al., 2020 ) , multi-modal lifelong navigation ( Khanna et al., 2024 ) , and active exploration for question answering ( Majumdar et al., 2024 ) . In manipulation, benchmarks evaluate multi-task generalization ( Yu et al., 2020 ; James et al., 2020 ) , object-level skill transfer ( Gu et al., 2023 ) , lifelong knowledge transfer ( Liu et al., 2023 ) , and everyday task scalability ( Nasiriany et al., 2024 ) . For long-horizon planning, benchmarks require agents to follow compositional instructions ( Shridhar et al., 2020 ) , interact through dialogue ( Padmakumar et al., 2021 ) , compose language-conditioned skills ( Mees et al., 2022 ) , handle diverse household activities ( Li et al., 2023 ) , and adapt plans based on visual feedback ( Tupini et al., 2026 ) . These benchmarks comprehensively cover perception, navigation, manipulation, and planning. Recent works further explore general-purpose embodied agent evaluation and realistic simulation environments ( Peng et al., 2024 ; Ren et al., 2025 ) . However, none is designed for evaluating the continual learning capability of skills in long-horizon tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 具身智能基准测试评估了从感知到长期任务执行的一系列能力（Liu 等人，2025a；Yifan 等人，2025；Liu 等人，2025b）。在感知层面，基准测试会考察三维场景理解（Wang 等人，2024）、空间推理（Du 等人，2024）、物理世界理解（Chow 等人，2025）以及场景动态变化（Wang 等人，2025）。在导航方面，该领域已从语言引导的导航（Anderson 等人，2018；Ku 等人，2020）发展为声音引导的导航（Liu 等人，2026）、物体定位（Qi 等人，2020）、多模态终身导航（Khanna 等人，2024），以及用于问答的主动探索（Majumdar 等人，2024）。在操作方面，基准测试评估了多任务泛化能力（Yu 等人，2020；James 等人，2020）、物体级技能迁移（Gu 等人，2023）、终身知识迁移（Liu 等人，2023）以及日常任务的扩展性（Nasiriany 等人，2024）。对于长期规划，基准测试要求智能体能够遵循组合式指令（Shridhar 等人，2020）、通过对话进行交互（Padmakumar 等人，2021）、组合语言引导的技能（Mees 等人，2022）、处理多样化的家庭活动（Li 等人，2023），并根据视觉反馈调整计划（Tupini 等人，2026）。这些基准测试全面覆盖了感知、导航、操作和规划。近期的研究进一步探索了通用型具身智能体的评估方法以及逼真的模拟环境（Peng 等人，2024；Ren 等人，2025）。然而，目前尚无任何基准测试专门用于评估智能体在长期任务中技能的持续学习能力。

paragraphs.en: Compositional generalization, the ability to recombine learned elements for solving novel problems, has been studied across multiple domains. In digital environments, benchmarks test whether mobile and web agents can compose atomic operations into multi-step tasks ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Furuta et al., 2023 ) . In video understanding, benchmarks study whether models can recognize unseen action–object combinations from separately learned components ( Li et al., 2024 ; Ahn et al., 2026 ) . For reasoning tasks, benchmarks show that models proficient in individual abilities still fail when these abilities must be combined ( Alazraki et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2025 ) . In embodied manipulation, benchmarks evaluate whether robot policies can generalize to unseen skill compositions after training on atomic skills ( Wu et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2025a ; Chen et al., 2025b ; Haresh et al., 2024 ) . In contrast, EmbodiedCLBench evaluates the continual learning capability in embodied simulation without any benchmark-specific training.
paragraphs.zh: 组合泛化能力，即重新组合已学习到的元素以解决新问题，已在多个领域得到研究。 在数字环境中，基准测试用于检验移动和网页智能体是否能够将原子操作组合成多步骤任务（Guo 等，2025；Furuta 等，2023）。 在视频理解领域，基准测试旨在研究模型能否从分别学习的组件中识别出未见过的新动作与物体组合（Li 等，2024；Ahn 等，2026）。 对于推理任务，基准测试表明，即便模型在各项单独能力上表现优异，当这些能力需要被组合使用时，它们仍然会失败（Alazraki 等，2026；Li 等，2025）。 在具身操控领域，基准测试评估机器人策略在基于原子技能训练后，能否泛化到未见过的新技能组合（Wu 等，2026；Chen 等，2025a；Chen 等，2025b；Haresh 等，2024）。 相比之下，EmbodiedCLBench 则在没有任何针对基准测试的特定训练下，评估具身模拟中的持续学习能力。

paragraphs.en: Evaluating compositional generalization requires a large combinatorial space of object–action pairs. We thus adopt TongSim as the simulation platform ( Sun et al., 2025 ) . paragraphs.en: Specifically, TongSim is a simulation with household scenarios and supports a wide range of interactive objects (such as cups, plates, cabinets, lamps, and appliances) and executable actions (such as walk to, look at, pick up, put down, open, close, and switch on, etc.). This simulation offers three key advantages: (1) the platform supports a large number of object types and action primitives, providing sufficient combinatorial diversity; (2) all scenes are indoor domestic environments, so that the tasks are grounded in meaningful, real-world household activities; and (3) TongSim has not been widely used as training data for existing foundation models, making it suitable for evaluating the generalization capability of agents with reduced risk of data contamination.
paragraphs.zh: 具体来说，TongSim 是一个包含家庭场景的模拟系统，支持多种互动对象（如杯子、盘子、橱柜、灯具和家用电器）以及可执行的动作（如走到、查看、拿起、放下、打开、关闭和开启等）。 该模拟系统具有三个主要优势：（1）平台支持大量对象类型和基础动作，提供了充分的组合多样性；（2）所有场景均为室内家庭环境，因此任务都基于有意义的真实家庭活动；（3）TongSim 尚未被广泛用作现有基础模型的训练数据，因此适合用于评估智能体的泛化能力，并降低数据污染的风险。

paragraphs.en: Our goal is to evaluate the capability of continual learning. However, it is an abstract concept that is challenging to measure directly. We operationalize it through compositional generalization: if an agent has learned from basic tasks, it should recombine previously mastered skill elements to solve novel tasks rather than learning each new task from scratch. This leads to a natural evaluation protocol—let the agent first complete simpler tasks to accumulate experience, then test whether it can leverage that experience to solve more complex, unseen tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的目标是评估持续学习的能力。 然而，这是一个抽象的概念，直接衡量起来颇具挑战。 我们通过组合泛化来具体化这一概念：如果一个智能体已经通过基础任务进行了学习，那么它应该能够重新组合之前掌握的技能要素来解决新任务，而不是从头开始学习每个新任务。 这引出了一个自然的评估方案——先让智能体完成更简单的任务以积累经验，然后测试它能否利用这些经验来解决更复杂且未曾见过的任务。

paragraphs.en: We design two levels of tasks based on atomic actions available in TongSim. Specifically, an atomic action is a single interaction with an object (e.g., “pick up the cup”). It consists of a sequence of steps (e.g., walking to the cup, looking at it, and picking it up), each of which is one executable action. Building on it, a basic task composes a small number of atomic actions into a practical household operation (e.g., “put the cup on the table”, which consists of “pick up the cup” and “put down the cup on the table”). Further, an advanced task composes more atomic actions than a basic task (e.g., “tidy up the room”, which requires picking up the book, putting the book on the shelf, closing the cabinet, and switching off the lamp). We provide more details in the benchmark overview (Section 4.1 ). All task descriptions are generated by Qwen3.7-Plus and manually verified for correctness (see Appendix B ).

paragraphs.en: For TongSim simulation, we chose its closed-source version, which provides more diverse actions than the open-source version. As a result, online simulation is not practical for the benchmark evaluation. Therefore, we construct an offline, reproducible evaluation process in the form of a state-transition graph, as shown in Figure 2 . A graph structure naturally represents the task procedure: at each state, an agent selects an action and transitions to the next state. This graph structure offers three advantages: (1) offline evaluation can be run in parallel without running the simulator; (2) flexible control over the task complexity through graph branching and depth; and (3) fine-grained analysis of agent behavior by checking each decision against the pre-computed graph.

paragraphs.en: With the task graphs built, we define how agents are evaluated on them. The evaluation consists of a learning phase and a testing phase. In the learning phase, the agent completes basic tasks to accumulate experience. In the testing phase, the agent attempts unseen advanced tasks with this experience. In this setup, basic tasks serve as the memory ( Xu et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) and test-time learning data ( Sun et al., 2020 ; Liu et al., 2021 ) for the self-evolving agents.
paragraphs.zh: 在构建任务图之后，我们定义了智能体在这些任务图上的评估方式。 评估包括一个学习阶段和一个测试阶段。 在学习阶段，智能体通过完成基础任务来积累经验。 在测试阶段，智能体利用这些经验尝试从未见过的进阶任务。 在这种设定中，基础任务对于自我演化的智能体而言，既充当记忆（Xu et al., 2026; Huang et al., 2026），也充当测试时的学习数据（Sun et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2021）。

paragraphs.en: For each task, the evaluation follows an interactive, multi-turn format: (1) the agent receives a task description and an image of the initial state; (2) at each step, the agent selects one action from a set of action candidates; (3) based on the action decision, the agent transitions to the next state and receives a new image with updated objects and action candidates; (4) this repeats until the agent reaches the goal (success) or exhausts the step budget (failure). The action candidates at each step are designed into three types: optimal actions that follow the shortest path, suboptimal actions that are executable but deviate from the shortest path, and invalid actions that cannot be executed in the current state. This interactive format preserves the sequential decision-making structure of embodied tasks while enabling fully offline, deterministic, and reproducible evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个任务，评估都采用交互式、多轮次格式：（1）智能体接收任务描述和初始状态图像；（2）在每一步中，智能体从候选动作集合中选择一个动作；（3）根据动作决策，智能体过渡到下一个状态，并收到包含更新后的物体和候选动作的新图像；（4）此过程重复进行，直到智能体达到目标（成功）或耗尽步数预算（失败）。 每一步的候选动作被设计为三种类型：遵循最短路径的最优动作、可执行但偏离最短路径的非最优动作，以及在当前状态下无法执行的无效动作。 这种交互式格式既保留了具身任务的序列决策结构，又实现了完全离线、确定且可重复的评估。

paragraphs.en: Figure 3 summarizes the overall statistics of EmbodiedCLBench . The environment covers diverse scenes, object categories, and atomic actions, providing a broad combinatorial space for task construction. The benchmark contains 268 tasks: 168 basic tasks and 100 advanced tasks. Basic tasks span six categories, with each grounded in a distinct type of daily household activity. Advanced tasks require substantially more atomic actions and shortest-path steps. The atomic actions of each advanced task come from two to four categories of basic tasks. Each atomic action consists of 3 steps. Therefore, the shortest path has 6 steps for a basic task (2 atomic actions) and 12 steps for an advanced task (4 atomic actions). With this scale, real-world grounding, and structured difficulty, EmbodiedCLBench can reveal meaningful differences in the continual learning capability of agents. Examples of basic and advanced tasks are provided in Appendix C .

paragraphs.en: We evaluate agents under three settings: (1) Zero-shot: the agent performs basic and advanced tasks directly, without a learning phase. (2) In-Context Learning (ICL): in the learning phase, the agent completes two related basic tasks for each advanced task. In the testing phase, the full interaction trajectories of these basic tasks are retained in context. (3) Skill Learning: in the learning phase, the agent completes the same basic tasks as in ICL. It then writes a concise skill summary of its experience in Markdown format. In the testing phase, only this skill summary is provided in context, instead of the interaction trajectories.

paragraphs.en: Table 1 presents the main results. Agents achieve a moderate zero-shot success rate on basic tasks (around 50%), indicating that current agents can execute simple household tasks. Zero-shot success rate on advanced tasks drops to around 10%, validating that advanced tasks are genuinely difficult. Both ICL and Skill Learning substantially improve advanced task success rate, raising it from around 10% to above 30%. This improvement is consistent across all harnesses, suggesting that experience from basic tasks can effectively transfer to unseen advanced tasks.

paragraphs.en: Compositional generalization is the core approach for evaluating continual learning in EmbodiedCLBench . paragraphs.en: As shown in Figure 4 (a), success rate decreases across all three settings as atomic actions increase from 3 to 6. Specifically, Figure 4 (b) shows that the gain over zero shot drops initially but then stabilizes at around 30%. At the highest complexity (6 atomic actions), zero-shot success rate drops to 4.0%, while ICL and Skill Learning still achieve 32.0% and 26.0%, respectively. This shows that experience from basic tasks still brings a substantial gain over zero shot, even when zero-shot agents can barely solve the tasks.

paragraphs.en: Results and Analysis. As shown in Figure 5 , the most substantial improvement occurs between k = 0 k{=}0 and k = 1 k{=}1 . A single learning sample raises the success rate from 8.0%–10.0% to 28.0%–40.0% across both harnesses and learning methods. This initial jump accounts for most of the total improvement across the k k range. Even minimal experience (completing just one basic task) provides sufficient new information for the agent to substantially improve on unseen advanced tasks. Beyond k = 1 k{=}1 , however, success rate does not continue to rise but instead fluctuates without a clear upward trend. This pattern remains across ICL and Skill Learning, and across both harnesses. None of the four curves shows consistent improvement with additional learning samples. This suggests that current agents cannot extract sufficiently distinct information from additional learning samples. paragraphs.en: The main results show that ICL and Skill Learning improve success rate, but do not reveal what agents actually learn from experience. We analyze how agents choose among these three action types. Instead of running new experiments, we use the selected actions recorded at each decision step in the main experiment (all four harnesses with Qwen3.8-Flash). Specifically, we compare the selection rate of each action type under ICL and Skill Learning with that in the zero-shot setting.

paragraphs.en: Results and Analysis. As shown in Figure 6 , experience sharply reduces invalid actions across all harnesses (by 13%–20%). Fewer invalid actions allow agents to stay on executable trajectories and reach the goal within the step budget. This suggests that the reduction in invalid actions contributes to the higher success rates in Table 1 . Meanwhile, optimal actions increase substantially. Suboptimal actions also increase slightly (by 3%–8%). Overall, experience shifts the selections of agents from invalid actions to optimal and suboptimal actions. ICL and Skill Learning show the same direction of change, but Skill Learning consistently produces smaller shifts across all harnesses. In contrast, Table 1 shows no consistent advantage between ICL and Skill Learning in success rate. This may reflect a difference in how experience is represented. Interaction trajectories may induce larger changes in decision behavior, while skill summaries may induce smaller but more focused changes.

paragraphs.en: Results and Analysis. As shown in Figure 7 , all three settings show a monotonically increasing success rate as the budget grows from 0 to 6 extra steps. This is expected, since a larger budget gives agents more room for suboptimal decisions. Across all budget values, the ranking of the three settings remains consistent. ICL achieves the highest success rate, followed by Skill Learning and then zero shot. This indicates that the gain over zero shot holds across different budgets. At the strictest budget (0 extra steps), zero-shot success rate is 0.0%, while ICL and Skill Learning still achieve 15.0% and 7.0%, respectively. Even under this strictest budget, learning from experience remains effective. Notably, compared to the zero-shot setting, ICL and Skill Learning exhibit a steeper increase in success rate as the budget grows. This indicates that the agents with prior experience can better benefit from additional tolerance. Meanwhile, the gap between experienced agents and zero-shot agents remains substantial even at the most generous budget (6 extra steps). This suggests that additional tolerance cannot replace the role of prior experience.
paragraphs.zh: 结果与分析。 如图 7 所示，随着预算从 0 增加到 6 个额外步骤，三种设置的成功率均呈现单调上升趋势。 这是可以预见的，因为更大的预算为智能体提供了更多做出次优决策的空间。 在所有预算值下，三种设置的排名始终保持一致。 ICL 实现了最高的成功率，其次是技能学习，最后是零样本设置。 这表明与零样本设置相比的优势在不同预算下均成立。 在最严格的预算（0 个额外步骤）下，零样本的成功率为 0.0%，而 ICL 和技能学习的成功率仍分别达到 15.0% 和 7.0%。 即使在这种最严格的预算条件下，从经验中学习仍然有效。 值得注意的是，与零样本设置相比，随着预算的增长，ICL 和技能学习的成功率上升更为陡峭。 这表明拥有先前经验的智能体能更好地利用额外的容错空间。 与此同时，即使在最宽松的预算（6 个额外步骤）下，有经验的智能体与零样本智能体之间的差距仍然很大。 这说明额外的容错无法取代先前经验所起的作用。

paragraphs.en: We introduce EmbodiedCLBench , the first embodied simulation benchmark for evaluating the continual learning capability of self-evolving agents. Our key idea is to formulate continual learning through compositional generalization: rather than solving each new task from scratch, an agent should accumulate experience from basic tasks and recombine previously acquired skills to solve unseen, more complex tasks. Following this principle, EmbodiedCLBench organizes tasks into atomic actions, basic tasks, and advanced tasks, providing a structured protocol for measuring whether embodied agents can acquire, retain, and transfer experience over time.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 EmbodiedCLBench，这是首个用于评估自我进化智能体持续学习能力的具身模拟基准。 我们的核心思想是将持续学习通过组合泛化来构建：智能体不应从头开始解决每个新任务，而应积累基础任务的经验，并重新组合之前获得的技能，以解决未见过且更复杂的任务。 遵循这一原则，EmbodiedCLBench 将任务组织为原子动作、基础任务和高级任务，从而提供了一种结构化方案，用于衡量具身智能体能否随时间推移获取、保留和迁移经验。

paragraphs.en: Extensive evaluations across multiple agent harnesses and learning methods reveal both promising progress and clear limitations: (1) Experience from basic tasks substantially improves performance on unseen advanced tasks over zero-shot execution, showing that current agents can transfer previously acquired knowledge to new compositions. (2) However, the performance of existing agents is far from saturation. Designing effective continual learning methods for embodied agents is a promising direction to explore. (3) Further, the benefit of learning does not consistently increase with the amount of experience. How to enable the agents to accumulate and exploit additional interactions is still an open problem. Overall, EmbodiedCLBench provides a principled testbed for studying self-evolution in embodied agents and highlights the need for stronger mechanisms that can continuously consolidate, generalize, and reuse experience across tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 在多种智能体框架和学习方法上进行的广泛评估揭示了既有令人鼓舞的进展，也存在明确的局限性：(1) 基础任务的经验能够显著提升智能体在未见过的高级任务上的表现，优于零样本执行方式，这表明当前的智能体能够将先前获得的知识迁移到新的组合任务中。 (2) 然而，现有智能体的性能远未达到饱和状态。 为具身智能体设计有效的持续学习方法是一个值得探索的有前景方向。 (3) 此外，学习带来的收益并不会随着经验量的增加而稳定提升。 如何让智能体积累并利用更多交互仍然是一个未解决的问题。 总体而言，EmbodiedCLBench 为研究具身智能体的自我演化提供了一个基于原则的测试平台，并凸显了需要更强大的机制来持续整合、泛化和跨任务复用经验。

paragraphs.en: Both task descriptions and action options are produced by a three-stage pipeline powered by Qwen3.7-Plus. The pipeline serves two purposes: converting low-level atomic actions into natural household scenarios, and ensuring that action options do not give away the correct answer through shortcuts. The key prompt specifications for all three stages are provided in Section B.1 .

paragraphs.en: Three annotators independently verify each generated sample. The verification covers three aspects: captured images, task descriptions, and per-state action options. For each aspect, annotators check for factual errors, logical inconsistencies, and whether the content reflects realistic household activities. A sample is retained only if all three annotators approve it.
paragraphs.zh: 三名标注员独立验证每个生成的样本。 验证涵盖三个方面：采集到的图像、任务描述以及各状态下的动作选项。 对于每个方面，标注员需检查是否存在事实性错误、逻辑矛盾，以及内容是否反映了真实的家庭活动。 只有当三名标注员全部批准时，该样本才会被保留。

paragraphs.en: We provide task examples at both compositional levels to illustrate the evaluation format. The agent first receives a natural-language task description. At each step, it observes the current-state image and selects one action from multiple candidates. Specifically, we include two basic-task examples (Figures 8 and 9 ; Tables 3 and 4 ) and one advanced-task example (Figure 10 ; Table 5 ).
